The inconsistent endpoint ordering in m117's 10/1 label remains unresolved and does not establish a physical negative-width mechanism.","batch_rationale":"The pending 16 already cover several aromatic esters, nitro carbonyls, salicylaldehyde, one new halogenated aromatic molecule, and additional strong-eluent conditions. These supplements add response segments around measured failures, connected exploration of four unobserved carbonyl molecules, a comparative alcohol set, and one focused loading-volume contrast. Same-load solvent comparisons are used where available; the m128 and m40 tests explicitly retain loading as a competing explanation. The batch avoids duplicate pending tuples and avoids spending labels merely to reconfirm already accurate loading contrasts. The m198 intermediate point, m205 strong-eluent point, and m128/m40 tests of apparent reversals address different ways a late anchor can fail to generalize. The new carbonyls and alcohol comparisons test whether those repairs transfer to neighboring structures across the Row-distribution. Selection does not maximize retention or interval width. Quantile widths are treated as uncalibrated outputs from one predictor; zero V1 lower quantiles and quantile crossings make width-only ranking particularly unpersuasive here. Expected improvement comes from teaching structure-condition relationships for both endpoints, with experimental variability and absent protocol variables remaining limits on mechanistic interpretation."}
